title: Monitoring edge-geodetic sets in graphs: the upper bound in terms of the feedback edge set number (Theorem 4.3)
author: Subhadeep R. Dev, Sanjana Dey, Florent Foucaud, Krishna Narayanan, Lekshmi Ramasubramony Sulochana
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem 4.3 (source0.tex lines 384--386, source label thm:fes), "If $\fes(G) \geq 2$, then $\MEG(G) \leq 9\fes(G) + |L(G)| - 8$ where $|L(G)|$ is the number of leaves of $G$", delivered together with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 387--420 (34 lines, a single adjacent proof environment that opens and closes inside the retained span). It is one of the article's two main structural results: the abstract announces that the paper "prove[s] an upper bound using the feedback edge set of the graph", the bound is the source of the article's Corollary 4.4 that $\MEG(G)=O(\MLN(G)^2)$ for every graph, and the article immediately notes after the proof that the bound is best possible up to constant factors, with a matching construction in its Proposition 4.5. The author proof is complete and self-contained apart from the two quoted lemmas it names. It fixes $k=\fes(G)$, describes a set $M$ of vertices of the base graph $G_b$ (all core vertices; one or two median vertices from every proper core path of length at least two; two or three non-core vertices from every core cycle chosen as equidistantly as possible), argues that every edge of a maximal hanging tree is monitored by leaves through the simplicial-vertex and cut-vertex lemmas, then verifies edge by edge that $M$ monitors the edges on core cycles (via the cut-vertex lemma and the cycle theorem) and on proper core paths (through the medians $x_1,x_2$ and the distance computation $d$ versus at least $d+1$ for any alternative path), and finally counts $|M| \leq 3n_c+2n_p+2k-2 \leq 3k+2(2k-3)+2k-2 = 9k-8$ using the quoted bound of at most $2k-2$ core vertices and at most $3k-3$ core paths, adding the $|L(G)|$ leaves by the retained Lemma 4.2. The construction and its verification, in particular the equidistant placement of two or three vertices on each core cycle and the worst-case counting over core cycles and core paths, are research-level graph-structural arguments rather than routine exercises, and the two quoted lemmas are named published results. H2: an original research theorem with a complete author proof of moderate length, resting on two quoted external results rather than on standard background alone.
